text: Lin28a/b are RNA-binding proteins involved in stem cell maintenance, metabolism, and oncogenesis, and are often overexpressed in poorly differentiated, aggressive cancers, though their role in tumor initiation versus maintenance was unresolved. In murine models, LIN28B overexpression alone was sufficient to initiate hepatoblastoma and hepatocellular carcinoma. Lin28b was also overexpressed in MYC-driven hepatoblastomas; liver-specific deletion of Lin28a/b reduced tumor burden, extended latency, and prolonged survival. Both intravenous Lin28b-targeting siRNA and conditional Lin28b deletion reduced tumor burden and prolonged survival, establishing a maintenance requirement. Mechanistically, Igf2bp proteins are upregulated, and Igf2bp3 is required for growth in the LIN28B-overexpression context. Across multiple murine models, Lin28b is both sufficient to initiate liver cancer and necessary for its maintenance.
